hero.title: About Indian Powerlifting Federation
hero.subtitle: Powerlifting India — Apex Governing Body Recognized by MYAS (Govt. of India) & Indian Olympic Association
hero.description: Founded in 1975 with the motto to improve national health through the Iron Games. Formally recognized in 1979 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports (Govt. of India) and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), and affiliated to the International Powerlifting Federation (IPF) and Asian Powerlifting Federation (APF).

mission.motto: Health and Strength for the Nation Through the Iron Games
mission.missionStatement: To govern, promote, and advance the sport of drug-free powerlifting across India. We provide standardized competition platforms, train nationally certified referees, and prepare elite athletes for international glory.
mission.visionStatement: To establish India as a dominant global force on the IPF World and Asian platforms while upholding 100% clean, drug-tested athletic sportsmanship.

pillars.title: 100% Clean Sport
pillars.desc: Uncompromising adherence to WADA and NADA testing codes across in-competition and out-of-competition testing pools.

pillars.title: Calibrated Platform Standards
pillars.desc: Olympic-calibrated Eleiko competition bars, cast steel discs, and certified combo racks for uncompromised safety and precision.

pillars.title: Grassroots to World Podium
pillars.desc: Systematic qualification pipeline progressing from District, State, and National Championships to Asian and World representation.

pillars.title: Democratic Governance
pillars.desc: Fair, transparent administration powered by 37 affiliated State Associations and 6 Central Public Sector Board units.

timeline.title: Foundation of Indian Powerlifting Federation
timeline.desc: Pioneering strength athletes and sports administrators came together to establish a unified national governing body for powerlifting in India.

timeline.title: Formal Govt. of India & IOA Recognition
timeline.desc: Formally granted National Sports Federation (NSF) status by the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports (Govt. of India) and affiliated with the Indian Olympic Association.

timeline.title: Unbroken Historic World Record
timeline.desc: Sri E.S. Bhaskaran lifted an astonishing 260 KG Deadlift in the 52 KG bodyweight division at the IPF World Championships — a monumental record in Indian sports history.

timeline.title: Expansion Across 37 State Units
timeline.desc: National membership expanded to all Indian States, Union Territories, and 6 Institutional Central Office Boards including Indian Railways and Police.

timeline.title: International Glory & 900+ Medals
timeline.desc: India successfully hosted 23 International Asian and Commonwealth Championships, won over 900 international medals, and secured 7 Arjuna Awards and 1 Dronacharya Award.

honors.title: Arjuna Awardees
honors.desc: Conferred by the President of India to legendary federation athletes for outstanding international sports achievement.

honors.title: Dronacharya Award
honors.desc: India's highest national coaching accolade awarded for sustained international podium coaching.

honors.title: International Medals
honors.desc: Gold, Silver, and Bronze medals captured by Indian athletes across IPF World, Asian, and Commonwealth meets.

honors.title: International Meets Hosted
honors.desc: Asian and Commonwealth Powerlifting Championships successfully organized on Indian soil with global acclaim.
